methodology: Admissions and student-success figures come from the schools’ Common Data Sets. Published values are reproduced as reported; cohorts and score-submission rates are shown because test-optional policies affect who submits scores. High-school GPA is not standardized between schools. Faculty degree figures use each school’s own published faculty population and are not a direct comparison.

metrics.name: SAT composite
metrics.interpretation: Middle 50% of first-year students who submitted scores; DePauw’s reported range and median are higher.

depauw_source.label: DePauw 2025–26 Common Data Set, section C

metrics.name: ACT composite
metrics.interpretation: Middle 50% of first-year students who submitted scores; DePauw’s reported range and median are higher.

metrics.name: Reported average high-school GPA
metrics.interpretation: The Common Data Set requests an average GPA, but high schools and colleges may weight or calculate GPA differently; treat this as context, not a standardized ranking.

depauw_source.label: DePauw 2025–26 Common Data Set, section C

metrics.name: First-year retention
metrics.interpretation: Share of the Fall 2024 first-time, full-time cohort retained by Fall 2025; DePauw reports the higher rate.

depauw_source.label: DePauw 2025–26 Common Data Set, section B

metrics.name: Six-year graduation rate
metrics.interpretation: Common Data Set rate for the Fall 2019 first-time, full-time bachelor’s cohort; DePauw reports the higher rate.

faculty.note: Both schools report 99% on faculty credentials, but the populations and wording differ. Faculty award programs also use different categories, so their counts are not ranked here.
